description: The Collatz map has one known attractor (4-2-1 cycle). Numbers with high delay are in the attractor basin periphery, analogous to pluripotent stem cells taking many developmental steps before committing to a cell fate.
mathematical_formalization: Attractor basin B = {n : Col^k(n) = 1 for some k}. Collatz conjecture: B = N+1. Basin depth at n is D(n). Numbers near the effective boundary (high delay) share properties with cells near bifurcation points.
analogical_connections: Waddington's epigenetic landscape: delay records are marbles on ridges
Stem cell pluripotency: high-delay numbers visit many states before converging
Neural attractor networks: each trajectory is like neural computation settling to fixed point
implementation_hypothesis: Visualize attractor basin as 2D embedding (log(n), D(n)). Identify effective boundary as locus of delay records. Test if boundary has fractal dimension > 1.
experiment_seed: Compute D(n) for n in [1, 10^7]. Create heatmap of D(n) vs n in binary. Look for fractal structure.
